newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: U.N. probes peacekeepers and child prostitution.
newsitem.headline: U.N. probes peacekeepers and child prostitution.

text.p: Secretary-General Boutros Boutros-Ghali has asked for an investigation into the extent of involvement by U.N. peacekeepers in child prostitution, U.N. spokeswoman Sylvana Foa said on Thursday.
The probe request was prompted by a paragraph in a U.N. report issued several months ago on the "Impact of armed conflict on children," she said.

One paragraph of the 96-page report, written by Graca Machel, widow of the late President Samora Machel of Mozambique, said children "may also become victims of prostitution following the arrival of peacekeeping forces."
She said that after a 1992 peace treaty ending a civil war in Mozambique, "soldiers of the United Nations Operation in Mozambique (ONUMOZ) recruited girls aged 12 to 18 years into prostitution."
A commission of inquiry confirmed the allegations and the soldiers implicated were sent home, she added, but did not say how many troops were involved.

"In six out of 12 country studies on sexual exploitation of children in situations of armed conflict prepared for the present report, the arrival of peacekeeping troops has been associated with a rapid rise in child prostitution," Machel said.

Foa said Boutros-Ghali was working with the U.N. department of peacekeeping operations "to find out how widespread is this problem -- is this isolated instances or is this something that we have to face every time we face a peacekeeping operation?"
She said it was U.N. practice to repatriate any peacekeepers involved in misconduct, as happened in Bosnia following charges of blackmarketeering and use of prostitutes.
"However, it is up to the national authorities to take disciplinary action. The U.N. does not have -- beyond sending them home pretty much in disgrace -- the capacity to take disciplinary action."
She noted the United Nations handed out manuals to national contingents containing general guidelines, on sexual behaviour and other issues.
"All peacekeepers must maintain the legitimacy of a peacekeeping operation and avoid any behaviour which can be construed as jeopardising their status," she said.
